title: Dismissal with immediate effect by the employer (CO arts. 337, 337c)

sources.title: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), consolidated version of 2026-10-01 (Fedlex); English translation, German text authoritative
Convention of this benchmark (not law): Study 4 SPEC.md item 6a

facts.question: Which employment-termination dispute does the claim concern? protected_period_notice: an ordinary notice of termination by the employer where the claim concerns whether it is valid or when the employment ends, because of the probation period, an incapacity through illness or accident, compulsory service, pregnancy or birth, or the notice period (CO arts. 335b, 335c, 336c). wrongful_termination: an ordinary notice by the employer that the claim contests as abusive (given for an improper reason, such as retaliation for claims or an employee representative's mandate), or against which the employee objects or claims compensation (CO arts. 336-336b). immediate_dismissal: a dismissal with immediate effect, without a notice period (CO arts. 337-337c).
Did the employer end the employment relationship with immediate effect, without a notice period?
Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the immediate dismissal in writing?

Does the employer give as the cause of the dismissal the employee's absence from work, and does the employee say they were prevented from working through no fault of their own (for instance illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation)?
Was the employment relationship agreed for a fixed term, with an agreed end date, rather than for an unlimited period?

Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?
Has the employee earned income from other work during the time the notice period or the agreed term would still have run?

documents.title: Letter or message dismissing with immediate effect
must_show: that employment ends with immediate effect
documents.why: CO art. 337c para. 1: The entitlement arises from a dismissal with immediate effect; the dismissal letter or message is the ordinary record that it was immediate and of its date.

documents.title: Employment contract or other record of its terms
must_show: Only if the file states that the employment was agreed for a fixed term: the agreed end date. Otherwise this item does not apply.
Only if the file states that a written agreement or contract sets a probation period other than the first month of employment: the probation clause. Otherwise this item does not apply.
Only if the file states that a written contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones: the notice-period clause. Otherwise this item does not apply.
documents.why: CO art. 337c para. 1: Damages run to the end of the required notice period or of the agreed term; the contract ordinarily shows the start date, any agreed end date, any probation clause and any notice clause.

documents.title: Salary statements (pay slips)
documents.why: CO art. 337c para. 1: Damages equal what the employee would have earned; pay slips are the ordinary proof of those earnings (and of the salary that caps compensation under para. 3).

documents.title: Employer's written statement of reasons
documents.why: CO art. 337 para. 1: Where the employee asked, the employer must give its reasons in writing; that statement is the ordinary record of the cause it relies on.

documents.title: Proof of the hindrance from working (medical certificate, or official order or summons for a non-voluntary legal obligation)
documents.why: CO art. 337 para. 3: Being prevented from working through no fault of one's own can never be good cause; a medical certificate, or the official order or summons for a legal obligation, is the ordinary proof of the hindrance and its dates.

documents.title: Written notice-period clause (individual, standard or collective contract)
must_show: end-point of the notice (e.g. end of a month)
the written instrument that sets it (individual, standard or collective contract)
documents.why: CO art. 335c para. 2: Damages run to the end of the required notice period; where a written contract varies the statutory periods, that clause is the ordinary proof of the period that applies.

documents.title: Proof of earnings from other work since the dismissal
documents.why: CO art. 337c para. 2: Damages are reduced by what the employee earned from other work; pay slips or contracts for that work are the ordinary proof of the amounts and period.

steps.title: Establish whether the employer dismissed with immediate effect
Record the dismissal, the contract and the salary
Establish the cause the employer relies on
Measure damages to the agreed end of the fixed term
Measure damages to the end of the required notice period
Record the document state for assessment

outcomes.title: Process ends: The entitlement arises only where the employer dismisses with immediate effect

presumptions.text: Convention of this benchmark (not law): A fact that the file does not mention is taken as not alleged, and the rules are applied as if it were absent. Silence never ends a process: where a fact's absence would end it, the unmentioned fact is unresolved. The defining event is never presumed: if the file does not mention it, it is unresolved. A fact that the file raises and leaves unsettled is open.
